concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: On 15 September 2026, the original DPA provision was still in force and required notification without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after awareness of a breach.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment's replacement breach-notification provision took effect on 1 October 2026 and reduced the deadline to no later than 24 hours.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment reduced the required prior written notice for routine on-site audits from 30 days to 20 days.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: As of 1 November 2026, the amended liability clause capped the Processor's aggregate liability at EUR 1,000,000, regardless of the EUR 700,000 in fees paid.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amended liability clause expressly states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality obligations.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd remained listed as an approved Sub-processor on 1 November 2026; its approval was not withdrawn until 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd's approval was withdrawn with effect from 1 January 2027, so it was no longer an approved Sub-processor on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, Personal Data locations were established in Norway, Estonia, Ireland, Lithuania, and Denmark.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: For a termination on 31 December 2026, the amended 60-day deletion or return period ends on 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and, in any event, no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach. the notice must include specified information about the breach and its consequences, and the processor must document breaches and cooperate with required regulatory or data-subject notifications.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and, in any event, no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach. The notice must include specified information about the breach and its consequences, and the Processor must document breaches and cooperate with required regulatory or data-subject notifications.
justifications: The amended breach provision establishes the 24-hour outer limit while retaining the immediate-notification duty and the original content, documentation, and cooperation requirements.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The incident involved confirmed exposure of usable privileged credentials, which triggers the expedited initial-notification regime.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness began at 17:10 on 9 April, making the 12-hour outer limit 05:10 on 10 April; the first notice arrived at 06:00, 50 minutes late.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: The follow-up report is due by the end of the third Business Day after awareness. After excluding the weekend and the 12 April closure, and excluding the Controller-approved pause on 14 April, the third counted Business Day is 15 April 2027.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The ordinary deletion deadline is 60 days after termination, but the later applicable deadline is the end of the tenth Business Day after the last hold ends on 25 August. Excluding the triggering date and the contractual closure date, that tenth Business Day is 9 September 2027.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: The backup contains no held records, so it must be deleted by the earlier applicable deadline. Thirty-five calendar days after its creation on 30 June 2027, excluding the creation date, is 4 August 2027.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: After termination, records retained under the hold and its post-release deletion window may be used only for legal preservation. The requested analytics use was rejected and no authorization exists for service delivery or analytics.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval could begin only after the proposed start date, written consent, and security review were all complete. The security review completed on 22 April 2027, later than the other conditions.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS was approved for transactional email from France and continued ordinary transactional email. Meridian Mail Ltd's temporary emergency permission did not reinstate authorisation for ordinary customer transactional email.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: Actual processing with effective authorisation existed in Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, and France, while Nordlicht's authorised Swedish infrastructure processing had begun. Denmark was withdrawn, and Finland, Germany, and Ireland did not meet both requirements on the relevant date.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees are EUR 1,140,000 after excluding VAT, the service credit, and the one-off training fee. Twice that amount, EUR 2,280,000, exceeds the EUR 2,000,000 minimum security cap.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year, and EUR 300,000 has already been paid for ordinary breaches in the same year, leaving EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary claim pays EUR 700,000 after its pool is reduced. The shared security loss pays EUR 1,750,000, while the two confidentiality losses pay EUR 250,000 and EUR 100,000 uncapped because confidentiality takes precedence over security.
